dataFields.name: Round
dataFields.validation: The request round this belongs to. Not required where the request is raised outside one as urgent (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Urgent
dataFields.validation: Set where the request is raised outside a round because something is needed at once (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Quantity
dataFields.validation: How many, in the item's own unit. Greater than zero (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Reason
dataFields.validation: 10 to 500 characters per item. What the approver reads before deciding to spend (BR-5).
dataFields.example: The two Grade 9 rooms have run out and there is a fortnight of term left.

dataFields.name: On hand
dataFields.validation: What the store currently holds, shown beside the item (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Below reorder level
dataFields.validation: Whether the item is already below its reorder level. Such items are offered for inclusion (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Estimated value
dataFields.validation: What the request is estimated to cost, shown to the approver.

dataFields.name: Requester
dataFields.validation: Whoever submitted it. Any member of staff may (BR-2).

dataFields.name: Withdrawal reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 250 characters. Required to withdraw a request.
dataFields.example: The store found a box at the back.

dataFields.name: Status
dataFields.validation: Submitted, approved, rejected, advanced, purchased, received or settled. The requester sees it throughout (BR-7).

businessRules.rule: At the end of the period Accounts open a request round and ask every member of staff for the supplies they need. A request may also be raised outside a round where something is needed urgently, and is accepted just the same.
Any member of staff may submit a request, and no stock permission is needed to do it. A lab teacher who has run out of a reagent must not need storeroom rights to ask for it.
Items already below their reorder level are offered for inclusion, so what the store already knows is short is not left out of the round by accident.
Each line carries an item and a quantity in that item's own unit. A quantity with no unit behind it is a number nobody can buy against.
Each line carries a reason. It is what the approver reads before deciding to spend, and a request with no reason invites a rejection.

Every request submitted in the round collects on one page for the School Admin, who sees all of them together in one place rather than one at a time. A round read one request at a time cannot be bought for in one order.

The requester can see the state of their own request throughout — submitted, approved, rejected, advanced, purchased, received, settled. A request that disappears into the office is a request nobody follows up.
Each requester submits their own request. The lab teacher submits theirs, and every other member of staff submits their own, rather than one person collecting everybody's list by hand.
Submitting a request buys nothing and moves no money. The decision to spend is a separate act.
A request may be withdrawn before it is approved, with a reason. After approval it is the approver's to reject or the purchase to complete.
A request is never deleted. A withdrawn or rejected request stays on the record, so a member of staff whose requests are always rejected is visible.

The goods are received into stock (UC-18-04).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Inventory → My stock requests → New request
basicFlow.userAction: Opens their own stock request and lists the items and quantities they need, with a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Opens a request against that requester. No stock permission is required.

basicFlow.navigation: New request → Set quantities and reasons
basicFlow.userAction: Enters the quantity for each item, in that item's own unit, and the reason for it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires a quantity above zero and a reason on every line.
Records it against the round, and buys nothing.
Gathers every request submitted in the round on one page for the School Admin, seen together rather than one at a time.
Shows the state throughout — submitted, approved, rejected, advanced, purchased, received, settled.

alternateFlows.condition: Something is needed urgently and no round is open
alternateFlows.navigation: Inventory → My stock requests → New request → Mark urgent
alternateFlows.behaviour: The request is raised outside a round and is accepted just the same (BR-1).

alternateFlows.condition: An item is already below its reorder level
alternateFlows.navigation: New request → Include a low item
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is offered for inclusion, so the store's own shortfall is not left out of the round by accident (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: The requester changes their mind before approval
alternateFlows.behaviour: The request is withdrawn with a reason and stays on the record (BR-10, BR-11).
No further request joins that round, and the collected requests go to the approver together (BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: Staff have not submitted by the closing date
alternateFlows.behaviour: They are reminded, since a round nobody answered buys nothing.

alternateFlows.condition: The requester wants to know where their request stands
alternateFlows.behaviour: The state is visible throughout, so a request does not disappear into the office (BR-7).

departures.requirement: There is no permission check anywhere on submitting a request. A lab teacher out of a reagent must not need storeroom rights to ask for it.
Every request of a round is presented on one page. A round read one request at a time cannot be bought for in one order.
The requester can see the state of their own request at every stage, from submission to settlement.
Submitting a request creates no advance, no voucher and no ledger entry.
Requests and rounds are retained 7 years, since the advance, the purchase and the ledger entry all reference them.

openQuestions.question: How often is a round opened — monthly, per term, or at the school's discretion?
openQuestions.assumption: At the end of the period as modelled. The period is not defined.

openQuestions.question: Where the same item is requested by several people, is it bought once against the round or once per requester?
openQuestions.assumption: Once against the round as modelled, and the report groups by item. Not confirmed.

openQuestions.question: Who estimates the value shown to the approver, and from what?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. No feature holds a price for a stock item.

openQuestions.question: Can a requester amend a submitted request, or only withdraw and resubmit?
Is an urgent request approved by the same route as a round request, or faster?
openQuestions.assumption: The same route as modelled. Urgency does not change who approves.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
